programmes.d: When convenience store employee Wanda Mason is found dead, investigators find the entire murder has been caught on the store's security camera. But the image of the killer is so degraded it seems impossible to positively identify him.
Police are suspicious of numerous bloodstains when a woman has a fatal fall down the stairs.
A man dies in his home after a long history of heart disease. A few weeks after the funeral, rumors surface that the death was no accident.
When an unsolved murder is reopened, a listen to the 911 call determines the murderer and motive.

How unlucky could one man be? His college sweetheart killed herself and fourteen years later, his wife ended her life in a similar way. Investigators had to determine if this was murder or simply a bizarre coincidence.
A flawed envelope is an unlikely clue to identifying a killer who laced a water cooler with cyanide.
An assistant manager of a Florida steakhouse is stabbed to death. It appears to be a robbery gone wrong, but a bloody fingerprint reveals that he knew his killer.
A clue no bigger than a thumbtack leads investigators to a trio of killers.

A twelve-year-old girl claimed she had been abducted and sexually assaulted. She recounted what happened in such a flat, unemotional voice that police found it difficult to believe her. Fibers on her clothing would prove she was telling the truth.
Scientific evidence casts new light on a 10-year-old disappearance.

Police are led on a wild goose chase when the wife of a prominent banker is kidnapped. An entomologist's unexpected discovery leads to a new suspect — and the realization that ordinary office equipment can leave extraordinary clues.
Tipster is found dead after revealing that a woman's death 16 years ago was murder.

A woman is killed while walking her dogs in the woods. Since she has no enemies and her husband has an alibi, police assume it's a hunting accident — until they find a strange letter, allegedly written by the woman before her death.
Woman suspected something wrong with her father flew back a thousand miles to find his home empty.

When Genell Plude is found dead in her bathroom, the scene points to suicide. But a coroner's inquest and a unique application of forensic science give investigators a different explanation for her death.
A man states that a robber shot his wife, but a song he downloaded makes investigators suspicious.

Several suspects and conflicting evidence complicated a brutal murder investigation. But the forensics were clear on one thing: the killer knew his victim, and that alone gave investigators a head start.
How did the stalker obtain the security system code for his victim's home? Police needed answers.
A surgeon is stabbed to death and the most likely suspect is seen in a restaurant at the time of the murder.
After inspecting storm damage to a home in Tampa, an insurance assessor simply disappeared.
In 1991, Dorothy Donovan was murdered in her Dover, Delaware home. When her son stated that she was murdered by a hitchhiker he had picked up, police were skeptical.
When a hit-and-run accident killed a high school athlete, everyone in town searched for the killer.

An aspiring model turned up dead and the prime suspect was her boyfriend. When he was eventually cleared, investigators had to dig deeper to find the perpetrator. With the help of a forensic geologist, they identified the most unlikely suspects.
A murder trail turned cold, until police got a call from a woman whose husband had a criminal past.
In 1991, Grand Junction, Colorado is on edge after a series of deadly bombings kill two people.

For years, a woman suffered from what appeared to be the unpleasant side effects of lithium, a drug prescribed to treat bipolar disorder. When she died, investigators had to determine if her death was due to natural causes, suicide or murder.
Lives changed in the 20 years following an unsolved murder, and so did forensic science.

A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has a perfect alibi. To determine time of death, investigators need to know when the victim ate his last meal. An endocrinologist, a forensic botanist and a short-order cook answer their question.
A lifelong resident in a Tasmania town was murdered. Robbery appeared to be the motive.

Police suspect Dr. John "Jack" Boyle in the disappearance of his wife, Noreen, when he signs mortgage papers for a new house with a woman pretending to be his spouse. The police later find Noreen's body in the basement of Dr. Boyle's new house.
When a wealthy socialite died after falling down the stairs, witness accounts contradicted evidence.
When a hit-and-run accident claimed the life of a high school athlete, everyone in town mourned his passing. Finding the killer was a long shot at best.
In 1997, Kelly Eckart's car was found, with her belongings still in it, but she was missing.

In 1995, the founder of American Atheists disappeared with one of her sons, her granddaughter and $500,000 in gold coins. The police investigated several suspects, including David R. Waters, who worked for American Atheists.
Forensics determines whether a woman's death in a fire is due to arson, murder or accident.

A married couple decided to escape the cold of winter with a mini-vacation in Key West. The wife went missing and police searched every square inch of the island; they found nothing but a pair of sandals which might have belonged to her.
A millionaire and his family were executed in their own home.
In 1991, Grand Junction, Colorado is on edge after a series of deadly bombings kill two people and injure one more. Police race to find the culprit before he strikes again.
The kidnapping of Adolph Coors leads to one of the most intense manhunts in US history.

A mother of two young children was found dead in her bedroom. Her death was ruled a suicide — but when investigators learned she had almost died in a house fire three years earlier, they decided to take another look at the evidence.
The development of technology could help solve a murder case that is twelve years old.
In 1996, Indiana police identified Richard Alexander as the “River Park Rapist” who assaulted four women that year. Later, DNA analysis casts doubt on his conviction.
Cutting-edge technology proves the police arrested the wrong suspect in a young girl's murder case.

In 2000, Christina Sanoubane was murdered in her Cedar Rapids apartment after moving away from her abusive boyfriend. There are clues at the scene: bloody footprints and DNA from the victim's rape kit.
In this case, it looked like the killer vanished into thin air...and perhaps he had.
When a Native American woman is brutally killed in the desert of New Mexico, her killers leave a crime scene rich in forensic evidence: tire tracks, shoe impressions and even the murder weapons.
Two men die of heart disease six years apart and each was once married to the same woman.

It was one of the most unusual cases in forensic history. Investigators had to find a way to solve a murder case using only a squashed tomato found at the crime scene and tiny, pinpoint reflections of light in a photograph.
Security cameras in a casino tracked a woman's movements until right before she disappeared.
A squashed tomato and a pinpoint reflection of light in a photo help catch a killer.
Soon after becoming pregnant by Dr. Maynard Muntzing, firefighter Michelle Baker's health quickly deteriorates. Eventually, she raises suspicions that Muntzing is doing her harm.
When a dedicated teacher disappeared, police had to determine if she was the victim of foul play.
In 1981, New York correctional officer Donna Payant disappeared and was later found in a landfill. The medical examiner not only identified the cause of death, but also found an important clue.
Seattle police had no suspects in the murder of a post-grunge singer for more than a decade.

In this international case of extortion, murder and stolen identities, scam-artist Albert J. Walker assumes the identity of co-worker Ronald Platt. Platt later turns up dead in an ocean with an anchor tied around his torso.
A grad student disappeared and a professor of geological sciences helped police in the search.
A young woman is stabbed more than 100 times. The killer leaves DNA behind, but investigators must play a cat-and-mouse game to obtain a suspect's DNA to match.
A man's wife kills herself 14 years after his college sweetheart commits suicide.
An investigation into the murder of Katie Poirier is stymied by the lack of a body. Finally, investigators use a single tooth found among some charred remains to identify her.
A woman, who had recently rejected a co-worker half her age, ends up dead in her driveway.
A serial killer was on the loose and police had to find him before he struck again. Their most promising lead was an unusual one: a bloody fingerprint on the body of one of the victims.
A pair of tennis shoes are found near a victim who had been stabbed on the beach.
When a woman went missing, friends and family were determined to find her. Their worst fears were confirmed weeks later when her body was discovered.
Three fingerprints on a window screen are enough for a print examiner to uncover a serial killer.

When police find the body of 11-year-old Krista Harrison, there are few clues to the killer's identity. But authorities are intrigued by unusual orange fibers embedded in clothing found near the victim.
With a long list of suspects, forensic experts agree that the killer in this crime knew his victim.

A human skeleton was discovered in the North Carolina marshlands. When investigators learned she'd been dead for 18 months, they knew it would be difficult to find out who she was, let alone who killed her.
A serial killer was on the loose and police had to find him before he struck again.
Tests reveal the race, eye color and hair color of the person who killed two young women.

A woman is found dead in a ravine, and crucial evidence has been washed away by severe thunderstorms. Twice, the trail turns cold. Almost 20 years later, an old hat and a chip of stainless steel brings the killer to justice.
A convicted arsonist claims his innocence and sets out to prove it.

When a wealthy real estate tycoon goes missing, it appears to be foul play. In his will, he leaves instructions in case he should die under violent circumstances — which were carried out after a hiker comes across his bullet-ridden skull.
A woman was brutally murdered in her home and the only witnesses to the crime were the family dogs.
After a Philadelphia Convention, 180 Legionnaires contract pneumonia-like symptoms and 29 of them die. The determination of one scientist helps identify the cause of this deadly disease.
The killer hoped to cover his tracks by staging the crime scene. But police saw through the attempt.
A lifelong resident of the tiny town of Lefroy, Tasmania was murdered outside his own home. Robbery appeared to be the motive, but with no suspects, the investigation came to a halt.
A young girl beaten after watching her grandmother killed, identifies the wrong person.
In 1996, Virginia Beach police arrive at the Makdessi apartment to find the bloodied bodies of Elise Makdessi and Navy sailor Quincy Brown. But was Brown Elise's lover or her assailant?
In 1984 police failed to convict the murderer of a college student.
The decomposed body of a young woman was discovered in a Bakersfield irrigation canal. If there was trace evidence, it had been washed away.
The body of a young woman was found a mile from her abandoned car.
Investigators find a shoe print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints at a murder scene. But they believe the most telling piece of evidence is the bite mark on the victim's chest.
A man vows to find the person responsible for the death of his sister.
In 1996, when a fundamentalist group begins robbing banks near Spokane, authorities know immediately that they are dealing with experienced criminals.
A husband and wife get shot, and their 16-year-old daughter manages to escape.
A teenager went missing after an evening of horseback riding. Her body was found a month later, three miles from her home. But the killer unknowingly left trace evidence behind.
A hairdresser was murdered. But the evidence at the crime scene didn't match any of the suspects.

When an elderly couple died in a suspicious house fire, their son became the prime suspect. Investigators turned to forensic science to determine if the fire had been set deliberately, or if it was an unfortunate accident.
When two women were found brutally murdered, police wondered if they were victims of a hate crime.

An obstetrician returned home from the hospital and found his wife on the bathroom floor. She was covered with blood and not breathing. He tried unsuccessfully to revive her, staining his clothes with her blood in the process.
An 18-month-old skeleton found on marshland puts forensics to the ultimate test.
When a talented television news anchor is shot to death outside her home, it appears to be a crime of passion perpetrated by an obsessed fan.
After shooting his victims, the killer placed the evidence into a bag and tossed it into the river.
On a windy Kansas night in 1995, a mysterious fire swept through the home of a prominent doctor. In the debris, investigators found evidence which told them how the fire started.
A woman's body is found inside a burned mobile home and the autopsy reveals she was beaten.
A security guard disappeared from his post without a trace; his remains were found a year later.

After a day of fishing in a quiet village in Switzerland, a teenage boy doesn't return home as planned. The investigation reveals some important microscopic evidence in the water near where he was last seen.
A college senior was found raped and murdered near an unpaved footpath.
When Rosemary Anderson is found dead on the side of the road, her boyfriend becomes the prime suspect. He eventually confessed to her murder, but so did another man: serial killer Eric Edgar Cooke.
In 2004, Mary Ann Clibbery was found brutally murdered in her Illinois business.
Flu-like symptoms of a mother and her children prove to be something more serious: thallium poisoning. After the mother's death, investigators turn their attention to finding the killer.
In 2006, Texas real estate agent Sarah Anne Walker was found brutally murdered in a model home.
